ui.chat.usage_reset.chip.role: chip control on a provider block's heading line
ui.chat.usage_reset.chip.tone: Short machine-adjacent label, sentence case, a numeral after a middle dot.
ui.chat.usage_reset.chip.note: Sits beside the account name inside the /usage panel's block heading; the dot and numeral are not prose. {count} is the number of reset credits left (a bare integer, no thousands separator). Keep it short enough not to push the heading's binding window out of its column.

ui.chat.usage_reset.chip_label.role: accessible name for the same chip
ui.chat.usage_reset.chip_label.tone: Plain, complete sentence; this is spoken, not drawn.
ui.chat.usage_reset.chip_label.note: A screen reader hears this instead of the short chip. {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account's label (an email or an account id). {count} is the number of reset credits still available (always 1 or more), and it is REQUIRED in the label: the visible chip draws the same number, and a spoken name that omits it fails WCAG 2.5.3 (label in name). One ICU plural on {count}; do not promise the spend here (the click opens a confirmation).

ui.chat.usage_reset.confirm_title.tone: Direct question, same construction as the surrounding dialog's questions.
ui.chat.usage_reset.confirm_title.note: {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. The confirmation appears inside the account's block, so do not repeat the panel's own title.

ui.chat.usage_reset.confirm_cost.role: the cost line under the confirmation heading
ui.chat.usage_reset.confirm_cost.tone: Matter-of-fact statement, not a warning; the action is reversible only by the provider.
ui.chat.usage_reset.confirm_cost.note: One ICU plural on {count} (reset credits still available, always 1 or more). It must state BOTH facts: one credit is spent, and the account's rate-limit windows are cleared. Translate as one sentence pair joined by a semicolon; do not split into two strings.

ui.chat.usage_reset.busy.role: in-flight explanation beside the inert confirmation
ui.chat.usage_reset.busy.tone: Calm, present tense; says the wait is the provider's, not a failure.
ui.chat.usage_reset.busy.note: Shown while the request is in flight; the buttons beside it are disabled. {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label.

ui.chat.usage_reset.busy_action.role: label of the disabled confirm button while in flight
ui.chat.usage_reset.busy_action.note: One word plus U+2026, matching ui.common.actions.retrying's shape. Keep it to a single word where the language allows.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_reset.role: result line after a credit was spent
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_reset.tone: Quiet confirmation of a completed action; one line, no exclamation.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_reset.note: ICU plural on {count} = how many rate-limit windows the provider cleared (at least 1). {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. This is the success arm.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_already_rede.role: result line when the same reset had already been applied
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_already_rede.tone: Plain, reassuring on the one fact that matters: no second credit was spent.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_already_rede.note: Reached when a retry carries the request id of an attempt the provider had already applied. {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_no_credit.role: result line when the account had nothing left to spend
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_no_credit.tone: Neutral fact plus the reassurance that nothing was spent.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_no_credit.note: {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. Do not add a purchase or upgrade instruction: this app does not sell credits.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_nothing_to_r.role: result line when no window needed clearing
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_nothing_to_r.tone: Neutral fact plus the reassurance that nothing was spent.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_nothing_to_r.note: {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. 'window' means a quota window (a five-hour or weekly rate limit), not an application window.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_failed.role: result line when the outcome is unknown
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_failed.tone: Candid and calm; it must not read as an error the user caused, and must not invite alarm.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_failed.note: The two clauses are both required: the credit's fate is unknown, AND asking again reuses the same request id so it cannot spend a second credit. {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. Never shorten this to 'failed'.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_refused.role: result line when the request was refused before anything was sent
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_refused.tone: Plain, factual; the important half is that nothing was spent.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_refused.note: {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. 'refused' names a pre-send refusal, not a provider rejection.

ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_unknown.role: result line for an outcome this app has no words for
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_unknown.tone: Neutral report of an unrecognised machine value; do not apologise.
ui.chat.usage_reset.outcome_unknown.note: {outcome} is an untranslated machine token from the backend (snake_case); render it verbatim. {account} is a provider name plus, when known, a middle dot and the account label. Do not translate {outcome}.
